Baimai logo concepts, round 1

Four concepts, each shown large, at about 60px and 18px, as an app-icon tile, and on light and dark. The wordmark is live Anuphan text for now; the final version will be outlined paths. Pick one, or mix parts, for example "3's letter with 1's vein".

3 · บ ใบไม้ (bo bai-mai)

Recommended

In the Thai alphabet, บ is recited as "บ ใบไม้", so the name is literally the letter's mnemonic. The mark is a looped บ whose last stroke sprouts a marigold leaf. It is rooted in Thai learning, it teaches the loop the app defaults to, and the leaf can sprout as the signature animation when a card is learned.

baimaiใบไม้
baimai

Trade-off: it's the most meaningful of the four, but non-Thai readers may see a "U" with a loop until it's explained. At 18px the loop closes up, so the favicon may need a simplified cut.

1 · Leaf card

A flashcard with one sharp corner, the leaf tip, and a midrib vein running across it. Card and leaf in a single shape.

baimaiใบไม้
baimai

Trade-off: the strongest at small sizes, but nothing in it is specifically Thai. On its own the shape could be any notes app.

2 · Fanned deck

Three leaves fanned like a hand of cards: ใบ counts both. The tones go from new (light) to mastered (dark), which mirrors the mastery scale in the app.

baimaiใบไม้
baimai

Trade-off: friendly and easy to read, but leaf fans are common in eco and wellness logos, so it's the least distinctive. Flag: a three-leaf fan sits near some cannabis iconography. Keep the leaves broad and smooth-edged.

4 · Looped leaf

A single leaf whose stem curls into the round head loop (หัว) that Thai letters start from. The "learner loop" detail of the font setting becomes the brand mark.

baimaiใบไม้
baimai

Trade-off: elegant and subtle. The loop is easy to read as an ordinary curly stem, so the Thai reference only lands once someone points it out. At 18px it starts to look like a ladle.
